detail.longDescription: For testing purposes and building my own understanding, I'd like to create a simple Django model and form that can result in a django.db.utils.IntegrityError when saved. Ideally, the error would be null value in column "foo" of relation "bar" violates not-null constraint or similar. I've tried creating a test model like the following: class ATestModel(models.Model): field = models.BooleanField(null=False) def __str__(self): return f'<ATestModel(field={self.field})>' and a test admin form like this: class ATestForm(forms.ModelForm): field = forms.NullBooleanField(label='field') def clean(self): return @admin.register(ATestModel) class ATestAdminWithErrors(admin.ModelAdmin): form = ATestForm But the form still validates the model and will give an error on the page: Please correct the error below. “None” value must be either True or False. How can I modify my example to generate a django.db.utils.IntegrityError when saved?
